decision.changed_angle: The prior earnings-versus-expectations thesis has no newly published catalyst. It is deliberately compressed to a brief side carryover, with the completed first full-session result reaction as context and no claim that the new price is a new operating development. Other selected stories are new Tesla governance, Airbnb earnings and Celsius rollout/retail reaction.

The Berkshire filing thesis is unchanged. The first completed-session price response changes the entry context but is not presented as a new catalyst. The entry is compressed to a brief side carryover, while the lead focuses on new retail/short-term-holder loss evidence and other side stories use a new merger and fuel-facility milestone.

Reuters' November19 report of record withdrawals from BlackRock's flagship bitcoin fund adds actual wrapper-flow selling after the November18 holder-loss/stress lead. This is a direct flow development that changes the adoption-as-price-floor assumption, rather than another price-only bottom call. The other three entries use actual Nvidia results, Gemini reaching search and OPEN's stated tokenisation initiative.

Reuters' November25 report of Meta talks concerning Google's chips changes the Alphabet angle from application/model adoption to a possible external custom-chip customer and competitive merchant opportunity. The lead explicitly keeps talks separate from completed deployment. This is a commercial-relationship development after the previous report cutoff, rather than a recycled Berkshire or Gemini adoption essay.
